name: Lottery numbers L(n,6,6,2) for n >= 71: fewest 6-number tickets that guarantee a 2-match prize (UK-lottery problem, past the published range)
compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days (constraint programming or SAT on a local model around a maximal independent set, as in Cushing-Stewart; checking an explicit design means scanning C(n,6) draws, about 1.3e8 at n = 71 and 6.2e8 at n = 90, which takes seconds to minutes)
statement: L(n,6,6,2) is the minimum number of six-number tickets such that every six-number draw shares at least two numbers with a ticket. Cushing and Stewart (arXiv:2307.12430) prove values through n=70, including L(70,6,6,2)=35. Their program calls the value 38 at n=71 a conjecture. The target is an exact value for some 71 <= n <= 90, with a working design and a checked lower-bound proof. Published lottery-design tables and compositions supply upper bounds, not exact values by themselves. This question differs from the bank's ordinary covering-design record target.
success_criterion: Success means the EXACT value of L(n,6,6,2) for at least one n with 71 <= n <= 90, established by both of the following. (a) An explicit list of L tickets (6-subsets of {1..n}) such that every one of the C(n,6) draws meets some ticket in >= 2 numbers, checked exhaustively. (b) A proof that no design with L - 1 tickets exists, whose computational part comes with a certificate an independent tool checks: an LRAT/DRAT proof checked by cake_lpr or drat-trim, a VeriPB proof, or an exact ILP infeasibility certificate re-verified in rational arithmetic. Any mathematical reduction must be written out in full or cited to a published lemma (e.g. Cushing-Stewart arXiv:2307.12430 Section 3). L must also be no larger than the live upper bound for the cell. Read that bound from coveringrepository.com ((v,k,t,m) = (n,6,2,6)), lottodesigns.altervista.org, and any later paper citing Cushing-Stewart, all re-fetched at claim time. Before claiming, the claimant must also check that no later paper has already settled the cell. The first target is n = 71 (L(71,6,6,2) >= 35 by monotonicity; the published program conjectures 38). Include the best valid composition of published objects for the same parameters and metric in the bar, even if it is absent from a printed table. State whether the candidate is a composition. Identify its components and composition rule. Values in unmerged pull requests are not bars.

partial_wins.statement: A certified lower bound: for some n in 71..90, a proof (same certificate standard as success criterion part b) that L(n,6,6,2) is STRICTLY greater than max(35, the Füredi-Székely-Zubor bound for n) and strictly greater than any lower bound published for that n after 2024-06-17.

A certificate-backed re-proof of a Cushing-Stewart value for some n in 60..70 (e.g. L(67,6,6,2) = 34 or L(70,6,6,2) = 35): an explicit design plus an LRAT/DRAT, VeriPB or exact-ILP certificate for the non-existence of a design one ticket smaller. The published proofs rest on an uncertified Prolog CP run, so this is the first independently checkable proof of that value.

verification_method: Upper part: parse the tickets and assert each has 6 distinct numbers in 1..n. Enumerate all C(n,6) draws, or equivalently build the graph G whose edges are pairs sharing a ticket and confirm that G has no independent set of size 6 (a clique search in the complement, run as a second, independent check). Lower part: run the certificate through its checker (cake_lpr or drat-trim for LRAT/DRAT, VeriPB for pseudo-Boolean proofs, exact rational re-verification for ILP), and confirm the encoding's generator matches the written reduction. Re-derive the reduction lemmas against Cushing-Stewart Section 3. Recompute the FSZ bound and the monotonicity bound. Re-fetch coveringrepository.com and lottodesigns.altervista.org for the cell, and search arXiv/Google Scholar for papers citing arXiv:2307.12430. Recompute comparison compositions using the same checker and resource metric.
status_checked: 2026-10-14; historical source check from supplied batch A material. Current sources were not re-fetched during preparation.
angles: Start at n = 71. The published program already reduces it to a few exceptional configurations (Figure 1 of arXiv:2307.12430: four 'bad (r,s)' tuples and one degree-pattern exception). Encode only those as SAT/CP with symmetry breaking, and emit LRAT or VeriPB certificates.

Re-implement the paper's local model (structure around a maximal independent set I, with |I| <= 5 forced because 6 independent numbers form a losing draw) in a certificate-producing solver (CaDiCaL plus LRAT, or RoundingSat/VeriPB) rather than Prolog CP. Calibrate by re-proving n = 66 to 70 first (partial win p2).

Equivalent form: L(n,6,6,2) is the fewest 6-cliques whose union graph on n vertices has independence number <= 5. The Turán-type and Shannon chromatic-index arguments in the paper are the obstruction side. Look there for the extra lemma that kills the n = 71 exceptions.

Upper side: a non-disjoint-union design with 37 tickets at n = 71 would also refute the program's conjecture of 38. Try local search seeded from the (14,14,14,14,15) union. Note that an upper-bound record by itself is already a covering-designs-record partial win (lottery (v,k,t,m) tables); here it counts only as part of an exact value.
Sweep n = 71..90 in order. L is monotone in n, so each settled value is a lower bound for the next. n = 90 (SuperEnalotto shape) is the showpiece cell.
pitfalls: Do not confuse L(n,k,p,t) (lottery designs) with covering designs C(v,k,t). The repositories write lottery designs as (v,k,t,m), with t the guarantee and m the draw size, so this entry's cells are (n,6,2,6).
The Cushing-Stewart lower bounds are not certificate-backed, and Bate-van Rees 1998 has known gaps. Do not cite either as a checker.
The FSZ minimum is over unequal partitions: the balanced partition overstates it.
The live repository value for (n,6,2,6) may already be below the disjoint-union bound. Read it before quoting an upper bound.
The Springer journal version (Constraints, 2024) was not read for this entry. Check it for any added values or corrections before claiming.
